Subject: Follow-up: capacity & pricing details from today's demo

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the demo today — great context. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can move procurement forward: 

- Expected steady-state usage: ~50,000,000 tokens / month (50M).
- Typical response size: ~300 tokens.
- Traffic profile: daytime peak with ~120 concurrent sessions, occasional short bursts up to ~220 concurrent.
- Throughput target: sustain ~10k tokens/sec, allow bursts to ~25k tokens/sec for short periods.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 150ms; p95 < 350ms for chat flows.
- Budget goal: aiming for ~$800 per 1M tokens (target unit economics we need to hit).

Key questions:
1) For Dedicated reserved capacity, what would you recommend for GPU type (A100 40GB vs H100 80GB) given our mix of mm-small/llama-family models?
2) Approximate committed size (number of GPUs) to meet the steady-state and burst profile above?
3) How does Redwood express price for Dedicated: flat $/GPU-hour + software fee, or can you quote an effective $/1M tokens for committed terms (we need that to evaluate our internal P&L)?
4) Any additional costs for autoscale/burst or model-variant fallbacks?

I've attached a small sample of our usage (FinVault_usage_samples.csv) and a blank SOW template. Procurement is on copy.

Thanks — Samir

On Mon, Apr 11, 2026 at 5:10 PM neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samir — thanks for the clear recap and the attachment. Looping in Ben (SE)...

Thanks — quick technical read below + a conservative config to meet your profile.

Assumptions / modeling notes:
- Average generation length: 300 tokens per request.
- Concurrency model: 120 steady concurrent sessions -> ~36k tokens/sec if all requesting simultaneously at 300 tokens each over 1s (peak instantaneous math). We model more realistically as sustained 10k tokens/sec with 2-3x burst headroom.
- Model family: you mentioned Llama/Mistral variants. These compress well with quantization (4-bit). H100 benefits for large context and mixed-precision; A100 is cost-effective if memory fits.

Throughput numbers (rough, benchmark-derived):
- 1x H100 (80GB) -> ~6k tokens/sec for medium Llama-family model (quantized), with efficient KV-cache and batching.
- 1x A100 (80GB/40GB variants) -> ~3.5-4.5k tokens/sec for similar model; depends on sequence length and batching.

Suggested committed config (conservative):
- Baseline: 3 x H100 (sustained ~18k tokens/sec) — covers steady 10k tokens/sec with headroom.
- Add 2 x burst H100 (on reserved-burst or autoscale) to hit short peaks ~30k tokens/sec when combined.
- Alternate lower-cost option: 6 x A100 (if A100 80GB available) — similar aggregate throughput but less headroom per-GPU and higher scheduling complexity.

Cost framing / $/1M tokens guidance (illustrative, to be formalized in quote):
- Dedicated model: we price committed pools as a combination of flat reserved GPU fee + platform consumption. For a 12-month commit with 3–5 H100 equivalent reservation, you should expect an effective $/1M-token in the ~$600–$900 range depending on model mix, quantization, and commit level.
- If you want a firm $/1M token number for budgeting, we can convert the committed GPU + software fee into an effective unit price and include it in the SOW.

Operational notes:
- Autoscale/burst: we offer reserved-burst capacity (additional pre-warmed slots) and pay-as-you-go burst; both can be included in the contract with separate burst budgets.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallbacks to smaller quantized variants are supported and don't incur extra infra fees beyond compute time.

I've attached a short PDF with the rough estimate and two configuration scenarios (redwood_dedicated_estimate_v1.pdf). Happy to jump on a deep-dive with your infra team to validate.

— Ben
